title: Tenant webhook dead-letter, replay tokenization, and throttle controller
creator: Samir Kapoor
description: Background: Customer-facing usage webhooks occasionally fail (timeouts, 5xxs, destination misconfig, transient network). We currently retry inline with a simple exponential backoff which causes long-lived failing deliveries to: 1) tie up worker capacity, 2) burn retries against tenant quotas, and 3) produce noisy SLO alerts. Goal: introduce a bounded dead-letter queue (DLQ) + replay system with tokenized, idempotent replay and a tenant-aware throttle controller so failing deliveries don't impact other tenants and replays are auditable and rate-controlled.
problem_statement: Failures to customer webhooks can overwhelm delivery workers and create noisy alerts. We need a DLQ with configurable TTL and size per tenant, a replay flow that uses replay tokens to guarantee idempotent re-delivery, and a throttle controller that applies per-tenant adaptive backoff while respecting priority tiers.
proposal: 1) On repeated failure (configurable attempts), move message to tenant-scoped DLQ (S3-backed segmented buckets + manifest). 2) Persist a compact replay token (sha256) and record idempotency key in delivery store so replayed deliveries are deduplicated by target and payload hash. 3) Expose replay API for console operators and an automated 'soft-replay' job that retries DLQ items with exponential backoff that factors tenant priority and recent failure rate. 4) Implement a distributed throttle controller: token-bucket per-tenant with dynamic rate derived from SLA tier, historical success rate, and current queue depth. 5) Add metrics, traces and a runbook for oncall to inspect and kick manual replays.
design_decisions: DLQ storage: S3 segmented by tenant + hour manifests to allow efficient scan and TTL-based compaction
Idempotency: use (tenant_id, webhook_url, payload_sha256, original_event_id) as dedupe key; replay token encodes manifest location + offset + dedupe key hash
Replay mechanics: keep original headers and X-Redwood-Replay-Token; replays must be marked and visible in usage audit logs
Throttle controller: central coordinator in DeliveryService with local cache; fallback to per-node token bucket if coordinator unavailable
Retention & TTL: default 30 days per tenant, configurable via org setting; short-circuit delete for manual purge requests
acceptance_criteria: DLQ accepts items after configured failure attempts and stores manifest entries in S3
Replay API can re-emit a DLQ entry and deliveries are deduplicated using idempotency keys
Per-tenant throttle controller enforces rate limits and prevents noisy tenants from consuming >X% of pool (configurable)
Observability: dashboards show DLQ size per tenant, replay success rate, and throttle events; traces link replay token -> delivery attempt
Runbook created and validated in oncall drill; a manual replay walk-through exists in Confluence
metrics_and_slos: Track: dlq_count{tenant}, dlq_age_p50/p90/p99, replay_success_rate, throttle_rejections, delivery_latency_after_replay. SLO: reduce worker queue saturation incidents attributed to webhook failures by 80% within 2 weeks of rollout.
implementation_notes:
- Add new DLQ writer in DeliveryService worker; write a compact manifest file per hour with entries: {replay_token, idempotency_key, target_url, created_at, attempt_count} (manifest is newline-delimited JSON)
- Small GC job to expire manifests based on tenant TTL and move older manifests to cold storage if retention exceeded.
- Replay API verifies replay token authenticity (HMAC with service key) and enqueues an idempotent delivery job.
- Update DeliveryService to consult ThrottleController before scheduling. ThrottleController exposes token acquisition API with rate feedback.
- Migrations: add idempotency index to deliveries table and a small background validator to backfill recent deliveries.
- End-to-end tests: mock webhook endpoints with deterministic failures to validate DLQ placement, tokenized replay, and dedupe behavior.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: DLQ scan cost for large tenants could be high — mitigate by manifest segmentation and paginated APIs
Risk: Replay token leakage could be used to trigger replays — mitigate by HMAC-signed tokens and short TTL for admin tokens
Risk: Throttle controller becomes single point of failure — mitigate with local fallback token buckets and leader election for coordinator
Risk: Idempotency key collisions on very high volume — mitigate with 256-bit payload sha and include original_event_id
open_questions: What is the default max DLQ size per tenant before we start auto-purging? (ops preference: 10k entries?)
Should replays count against tenant billing (yes/no)? Current thinking: replays should not consume billed 'ingestion' but should be rate-limited by quota
Do we expose manual replay controls in Console or restrict to API/troubleshooter roles only?
How do we surface failed webhook payloads securely to the console without exposing PII? (link preview + redact)
